_note: Our own writing, rules from the core book (page refs). The guided first campaign opening (DESIGN.md section 8): a Union training base, a briefing (the book starts every first session with one, Core p.40), a live-fire drill against training drones that teaches one thing at a time, then the debrief, level up and a first downtime at the base. Lessons run in order; each shows when its topic first comes up (show_on) and is done when the pilot does it (done_on). 'tips' are one-off explanations shown the first time something happens, whatever lesson is running. Event types and fields: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and src/story/README.md. 'mine' = the event's unit is one of the player's.

lessons.title: Welcome, rookie
lessons.text: You're a new pilot at License Level 0 (LL0). Everyone starts here: you fly the GMS Everest, the standard Union frame, with standard gear. Every mission you finish, win or lose, raises your License Level by one. Each mission starts with a briefing: what's happening, what you're trying to do, and what's at stake.

lessons.title: Reserves
lessons.text: Before you deploy, you establish your RESERVES: anything extra you bring to this mission, like spare repairs, a favor, intel or a ride. Reserves last one mission. You don't have any yet; you earn them through downtime and from people who owe you.

lessons.title: Turns and actions
lessons.text: Combat runs in rounds. Your side and the enemy's take turns picking who acts next, and the players decide among themselves who goes. On your turn you get a standard move plus either two quick actions or one full action. You can't take the same action twice in one turn.

lessons.title: Moving
lessons.text: Your standard move lets you move up to your SPEED in spaces. Plan with the movement arrow, then confirm. Moving next to an enemy ENGAGES you; moving away from an engaged enemy later can provoke a reaction.

lessons.title: Attacking
lessons.text: SKIRMISH (a quick action) attacks with one weapon. Roll d20 plus your bonuses against the target's EVASION; 20+ is a critical hit that rolls damage twice and keeps the best. The pop-up number shows the math: hover it for the breakdown.

lessons.title: Cover
lessons.text: Anything between an attacker and its target can give cover. SOFT cover (smoke, trees, low walls) gives ranged attacks +1 Difficulty; HARD cover (buildings, tall walls, wrecks) gives +2 Difficulty, but only if you're right next to it and no bigger than it. Cover doesn't stack.
lessons.objective: End a move next to hard cover, or shoot at a target behind some.

lessons.title: Heat
lessons.text: Some weapons and systems build HEAT. If your heat goes past your HEAT CAP you overheat: you take 1 STRESS, make an overheating check, and your heat clears (any extra heat carries over). OVERCHARGE gives you an extra quick action this turn for heat (1d3 the first time, more each time). STABILIZE (a full action) can cool you down.
lessons.objective: Try Overcharge for an extra quick action, and watch your heat.

lessons.title: Tech actions
lessons.text: Not every action is a gun. LOCK ON (quick action) marks a target so the next attack against it gains +1 Accuracy. SCAN shows an enemy's stats. Tech attacks roll against E-DEFENSE instead of Evasion.
lessons.objective: Lock On to a drone, then attack it.

lessons.title: Damage and structure
lessons.text: Damage comes off your HP after ARMOR. At 0 HP you lose a point of STRUCTURE, your HP refills, and you roll on the structure damage table. Most mechs have four structure; lose them all and the mech is destroyed. Your pilot can still eject or get out.

lessons.title: Finish the fight
lessons.text: That's the core of it. Put everything together: move to cover, lock on, attack, keep your heat in check. Win or lose, everyone levels up after the mission.

lessons.title: Leveling up
lessons.text: After every mission each pilot goes up one License Level and gets +2 to a trigger, +1 to a mech skill, a talent rank and a license rank. License ranks unlock other manufacturers' frames and gear: rank II of a frame's license lets you fly that frame.
lessons.objective: Pick a trigger and a mech skill.

lessons.title: Downtime: talk to people
lessons.text: Between missions there's downtime. Walk around the base (WASD or click), and talk to people (F or click them). Conversations can unlock contacts, jobs and help for the next mission. Some replies need a skill trigger your pilot has.
lessons.objective: Talk to someone at the base.

lessons.title: Your downtime action
lessons.text: Each pilot usually gets one downtime action between missions: get connected, get a damn drink, scrounge and barter, and more. Each rolls d20 plus a trigger that fits and gives a result for 9 or less, 10-19 or 20+. What you gain becomes reserves for the next mission. Open the list with Tab.

lessons.title: On to the real thing
lessons.text: When everyone's done, end downtime and pick your next job from the board. From here on, the GM builds missions for you. Teaching hints stay on until you switch them off.
lessons.objective: End downtime and choose a job.

tips.title: Engaged
tips.text: Moving next to a hostile character ENGAGES you both. Engaged characters get +1 Difficulty on ranged attacks, and being engaged by something your size or bigger stops your move. Starting a move within an enemy's threat can provoke Overwatch.

tips.title: Reactions
tips.text: A reaction is something you can do outside your turn when its trigger happens, like Brace or Overwatch. You get one reaction per turn.

tips.title: Structure lost
tips.text: That mech hit 0 HP: it lost one STRUCTURE, its HP refilled, and it rolled on the structure damage table.

tips.title: Overheated
tips.text: Heat went past the HEAT CAP: 1 STRESS lost, an overheating check, and heat cleared. A mech at 0 STRESS melts down at the end of its next turn.

tips.title: Critical hit
tips.text: 20 or more on an attack is a critical hit: damage dice are rolled twice and the best results kept.

tips.title: A miss
tips.text: Missed? Accuracy helps: Lock On gives +1 Accuracy on the next attack against that target. Difficulty (from cover or being engaged) hurts.

tips.title: Skill checks
tips.text: Out of the mech, things that could go wrong are skill checks: d20 plus one trigger that fits, 10 or more succeeds. RISKY checks have consequences under 20; HEROIC ones need 20.

tips.title: You gained a reserve
tips.text: That's yours for the next mission only. It shows under your pilot on the left.
